title: Mautohe Cathedral Cove Track: Hahei area, Coromandel
overview: This popular walk has spectacular views over the pristine waters of Te Whanganui-o-Hei Marine Reserve. It ends at the iconic rock archway.

For fares and timetables, see Cathedral Cove Park & Ride .
It takes 30 min to walk from the car park to the track entrance. There's a long uphill section with little shade.
Tidal access: At high tide, Mautohe Cathedral Cove beach can be cut off from the track. Keep an eye on the tide and do not enter the rock archway if it's underwater.
Boats and watercraft: There are no boat lanes to separate boats, jet skis and kayaks from swimmers. Stay alert in and around the water.
At low tide, there's more room on the beach and it's easier to stay clear of the cliffs.

Bookings are not required for Mautohe Cathedral Cove Track.
Non-flushing toilets and an accessible toilet are located at the track entrance. There are flush toilets (non-accessible) on the track 10–15 min walk from the beach.
Don't feed fish - it disturbs their natural behaviour.
The Broken Hills Campsite is located beside the Tairua River among native bush. This is a standard campsite in the Coromandel region.
